intro: Tirana rewards visitors with vibrant streets, warm hospitality, and a growing food scene. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro or tram; city buses are the main public transport.
Single bus ticket costs 40 lek, sold on board by a conductor.
Taxis: flag-fall 300 lek, cross-town ride 400–800 lek; demand the meter.
Ride apps: Speed Taxi, Patoko, Clust, VrapOn Taxi Albania work like Uber.
Walking is best in the compact centre; sidewalks can be uneven.
Bike lanes exist on some main streets; cycling can be risky due to traffic.

skanderbeg.name: Skanderbeg Square
skanderbeg.tip: Start here to get your bearings. The square is car-free and best at dusk when the lights come on.

pyramid.name: Enver Hoxha Pyramid
pyramid.hours: Always open · interior access varies, check on the day
pyramid.tip: The concrete shell is a favourite for photos. Climbing is unofficial and slippery, so stay on the ground.

bunkart1.name: Bunk'Art 1 Museum
bunkart1.price_text: Small entry fee; check the current price on the day
bunkart1.hours: Usually daily, roughly 09:00–16:00 or later in summer; check on the day
bunkart1.tip: A huge Cold War bunker with long tunnels. Wear flat shoes and allow more time than you think.

historical-museum.name: National Historical Museum
historical-museum.price_text: Small entry fee; check on the day
historical-museum.hours: Typically Tue–Sun, closed Monday; check on the day
historical-museum.tip: The mosaic on the facade is worth a look alone. Inside, the communist-era rooms explain a lot of the city.

ethem-bey.name: Ethem Bey Mosque
ethem-bey.hours: Open around prayer times; closed to visitors during prayers
ethem-bey.tip: Small and beautifully painted inside. Cover shoulders and legs, and take shoes off at the door.

cathedral.name: Resurrection of Christ Orthodox Cathedral
cathedral.hours: Usually open daytime; check on the day
cathedral.tip: The bell tower and dome are striking from outside. Dress modestly if you go in.

kruje-castle.name: Krujë Castle
kruje-castle.price_text: Castle grounds free; museum inside has a small fee
kruje-castle.hours: Grounds usually open daily; museum hours vary, check on the day
kruje-castle.tip: A half-day trip from Tirana. The old bazaar below the walls is good for souvenirs and a coffee.

tave-kosi.name: Tavë Kosi
tave-kosi.price_text: ≈ 500–900 ALL per plate at a local restaurant
tave-kosi.hours: Served at lunch and dinner in most traditional restaurants
tave-kosi.tip: Albania's baked lamb and yogurt dish. Try it at a traditional restaurant near the centre, not a tourist cafe.

new-bazaar.name: New Bazaar (Pazari i Ri)
new-bazaar.price_text: Free to browse; food priced per item
new-bazaar.hours: Market roughly morning to early evening; cafes later
new-bazaar.tip: Come in the morning for produce and cheese. The surrounding streets have good cheap lunches.

dajti-express.name: Dajti Express cable car
dajti-express.price_text: Return ticket; check the current price on the day
dajti-express.hours: Usually daily, roughly 09:00–19:00; check on the day
dajti-express.tip: Ride up for views over the whole city. Bring a jacket, it is cooler at the top.

blloku-walk.name: Blloku neighbourhood walk
blloku-walk.hours: Always open; liveliest in the evening
blloku-walk.tip: Once the communist elite's closed district, now the city's cafe and bar hub. Wander the side streets after dark.

rruga-kavajes.name: Rruga e Kavajës stroll
rruga-kavajes.tip: A long central avenue with shops and cafes. Good for an easy walk between the centre and the river.

free-walking-tour.name: Free walking tour of Tirana
free-walking-tour.price_text: Free; tip the guide (≈ 1000–2000 ALL is usual)
free-walking-tour.hours: Usually one or two departures daily; check on the day
free-walking-tour.tip: Meet near Skanderbeg Square. A good way to learn the city's history in two hours.

grand-park.name: Grand Park of Tirana
grand-park.tip: Big green space with a lake and paths. Rent a bike or just walk; locals come here to cool off.

artificial-lake.name: Artificial Lake viewpoint
artificial-lake.tip: Walk the lakeside path for city views and a quiet break from the traffic.

blloku-bars.name: Blloku bar street
blloku-bars.price_text: Drinks priced per bar; expect mid-range for the city
blloku-bars.tip: Pick a bar with locals inside rather than the first one you see. Prices vary a lot street to street.

byrek.name: Byrek and coffee stop
byrek.hours: Bakeries usually open early morning to evening
byrek.tip: Cheap, filling and everywhere. Grab a warm cheese or spinach byrek for breakfast.

bunkart2.name: Bunk'Art 2
bunkart2.price_text: Small entry fee; check on the day
bunkart2.hours: Usually daily; check on the day
bunkart2.tip: A smaller city-centre bunker museum about surveillance and the secret police. Easier to fit in than Bunk'Art 1.

komuna-parisit.name: Komuna e Parisit cafe walk
komuna-parisit.price_text: Free to walk; cafes priced per order
komuna-parisit.hours: Cafes usually open morning to late
komuna-parisit.tip: A local residential area with good coffee and fewer tourists. Pair it with the Grand Park.

raki-tasting.name: Raki and Albanian food tasting
raki-tasting.price_text: ≈ 1500–3000 ALL per person depending on venue
raki-tasting.tip: Raki is strong; sip it slowly with mezze. Ask what is local and in season.

day-trip-berat.name: Day trip to Berat
day-trip-berat.price_text: ≈ 3000–6000 ALL per person by shared tour; check inclusions
day-trip-berat.tip: A UNESCO town of stacked white houses. Confirm transport and guide are included before booking.

clock-tower.name: Tirana Clock Tower
clock-tower.price_text: Small fee to climb; check on the day
clock-tower.hours: Usually daytime; check on the day
clock-tower.tip: Right by the mosque. A short climb for a view over the square.

mother-teresa-square.name: Mother Teresa Square walk
mother-teresa-square.tip: A wide square near the university and the Pyramid. Good for an evening stroll.

plans.for: One easy day on foot: the square, the Pyramid and Blloku, with a cable car view if the sky is clear.

styles.blurb: Byrek, tavë kosi and long café mornings.

stays.why: Walk to the main sights, museums and the airport bus; best for a first short stay.
Bars, restaurants and cafés on your doorstep; lively at night, a short walk to the centre.
Quieter street with mid-range hotels; 10–15 minutes on foot to the square.
Local, cheaper and near the big park and cable car; use buses or taxis to the centre.

food: Start the day with byrek (flaky pastry with cheese or spinach) and a strong coffee, roughly 100–200 lek.
Try tavë kosi (baked lamb with yogurt) and fërgesë (peppers, tomato and cheese) at a traditional restaurant.
Blloku has the densest cluster of cafés and restaurants; walk a block off the main street for better prices.
Cheap eats: grilled meat, suflaqe (wraps) and bakery snacks for about 300–600 lek a meal.
Coffee culture is serious here. A macchiato at a local bar is often under 100 lek; sit and linger.
more_time: Swap a city day for Krujë: buses run from the north terminal, about an hour each way, for the castle and old bazaar. Check times on the day.
Add a day trip to Berat or Gjirokastër by bus or hired car; both are long day trips, so an overnight is better.
Ride the Dajti Ekspres cable car from the east edge of the city for views over Tirana; check opening hours on the day.
